notes.decision: Puzzling form. Best parse: Lyc habitual prefix ϣⲁⲓ̈- (1sg) + verbal compound ending in ⲣⲁⲕ 'still' (cf. ϩⲣⲁⲕ/ⲍⲣⲁⲕ 'be still'). The intervening ϩ̄ⲡⲥ̄ may represent ⲣ̄- + abbreviated nominal element. Confirmed by line 28 [ⲉⲓ̈]ϩⲁⲣⲕ ϩⲙ̄ ⲡⲁϩⲏⲧ 'I am still in my heart' which is the answering state-description of the same chapter's question.

Greek πολιτεύεσθαι 'conduct one's life as a citizen' (cf. accumulated vocabulary ⲁⲡⲟⲗⲓⲧⲉⲩⲉ). Here in the disciple's self-description: 'I conduct myself in [a manner befitting] my works' — the harmonious state when the soul is at peace.

Rendered 'my other body has come to ease upon me.' The verb ⲁⲥⲓⲱⲣ parallels ⲁⲥⲓⲱⲩ in line 24 (where the body 'is light upon me'); both describe the comfortable bodily state. Likely Lyc variants of a verb of bodily ease/lightness, contrasting with ⲧⲱⲗⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲓ̈ 'weighs upon me' (line 18) in the disturbed state. ⲡⲁⲕⲉⲥⲱⲙⲁ 'my other body' likely refers to the spiritual/inner body distinct from the flesh-body — Manichaean anthropological dualism.

Rendered 'my Arche.' Greek ἀρχή ('beginning, principle, dominion') as a Manichaean technical term — likely the inner ruling principle or divine origin within the speaker, paired here with the 'other body' as the higher faculty that rejoices in Wisdom. Retained as 'Arche' to preserve the technical Greek register.

Parsed as ⲙⲁⲓ̈- (negative habitual 1sg) + ⲟⲛⲑⲁⲙ (Lyc reflex of ϣⲛ̄-ϭⲟⲙ 'find power/be able'). The reduced ⲟⲛ- for ϣⲛ̄- and ⲑⲁⲙ for ϭⲟⲙ are dialectal. Renders 'I do not have the power-of-heart' = 'I am not able with my heart.'

ⲑⲃⲓⲟ 'humble, abase' + 3pl object suffix -ⲁⲩ = 'humble them' — referring to the disturbing teachings/reflections that have arisen. The speaker cannot put them down at the moment of disturbance. Direct object reading preferred over reflexive.

Lyc reduplicated intensive ϩⲁⲣⲟⲓ̈-ϩⲁⲣⲟⲓ̈ 'of myself, by my own self.' Rendered 'of themselves' here since the subject is plural (the awakening teachings) and the reflexive is grammatically attached to 'in my heart again'; the sense is that the disturbances arise spontaneously/autonomously rather than being externally implanted.

Preserved literally with interpuncts. Meaning unclear: possibly an abbreviation, a ditto/repetition marker, a liturgical interjection, or a scribal feature. Could potentially complete the verb begun by ϣⲁⲓ̈- at end of line 15 ('I habitually do · aa ·'). The interpuncts may signal foreign/quoted material or an editorial-textual marker. Flagged for parallels.

Reduplicated qualitative on root ⲥⲣϥ̄- 'be loose, idle, disjointed' (cf. ⲥⲗⲱϥⲗⲉϥ 'flabby, loose'). Modifies ⲡⲁⲥⲉϫⲉ 'my speech.' Rendered 'is dilatory' — capturing both the slackness and disorderliness of disturbed speech. Could alternatively be 'scattered/dispersed.'

ϣⲁⲓ̈- (habitual 1sg) + ⲣ̄- + ϣⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲧⲓⲡ (reduplicated form, possibly 'be turned-down, prostrated' or 'be cast about'). The ϣⲧⲣ- element echoes ϣⲧⲣ̄ⲧⲣ̄ 'disturbance.' Rendered 'I am habitually undone' — capturing the disturbed/overthrown state in line with the surrounding affliction-vocabulary.

Rendered 'my way.' ϫⲓⲛ likely the Coptic nominalizing prefix substantivized = 'manner, way of being.' ⲡⲁϫⲓⲛ ⲧⲏⲣϥ̄ 'my whole way.' Could alternatively be ϭⲓϫ 'hand' but the construction 'cut off in my whole hand' is awkward.

Greek loanword pair πολιτεύω/πολιτεία = 'conduct life as a citizen / mode of life.' Rendered 'conduct myself in the conduct.' The verbal-nominal cognate pair preserved in English to mirror the Coptic figura etymologica.

'These two matters' — referring to the disciple's two-part question about (1) why his body alternates between disturbance and peace, and (2) what these states correspond to. The numbering 'two' confirms the structural binary that organizes the entire confession.

Anomalous closing bracket at end of line 4 without preceding opening bracket. Treated as transcription artifact; the word ⲧⲉⲡⲓⲑⲩⲙⲓⲁ '(the) desire' (Greek ἐπιθυμία with definite article ⲧ-) is split across lines 4-5 in standard Coptic word-division, with the orthography possibly omitting the medial -ⲓ- between ⲡ and ⲑ.
Translated 'wears the body' preserving the Greek loan φορεῖν 'wear/bear (as garment)' as in glossary entry ⲣⲫⲟⲣⲉ. The soul wears the body as a garment — standard Manichaean somatic register.
Translated 'unto her' per glossary entry ⲍⲓⲣⲉⲧ⸗ 'unto (the feet of)'; here with 3sg.f suffix, marking the soul as object of the Mind of Light's salvific arrival.

Both verbs are 3sg.m habitual + 3sg.f object: 'he establishes her, he purifies her.' The actor is the Mind of Light (line 2); the object is the soul. ⲥⲁⲧϩ̄ = ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄/ⲥⲁⲑⲏⲧ 'set, fix' or possibly a Lyc establish-stem (cf. ⲉⲥⲥⲁⲧϩ̄ line 26 of food being 'established'). ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲁⲥ = ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲟ-ⲥ̄ 'purify her.'

Tentatively rendered 'shock.' The lexeme stands in a triadic series with ⲱⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'disturbance' and ⲧⲁⲣⲁⲭⲏ 'tarachē', all denoting agitation. Possibly Lyc form related to ⲧⲱϩⲥ̄ 'strike, smite.' Confidence low.
ⲛⲉϩ- (Lyc 'his') + ⲍⲱⲁⲟⲛ (Greek ζῷα plural 'living-creatures'). In cosmological context here = his cosmic living-creatures = the zodiacal animal-figures, paired with 'his stars on high.'

Translated 'grief.' Recurring on this page (lines 9, 16, 22) in triadic series with ⲧⲃⲁⲕⲉ 'bitterness' and ⲧⲁⲩⲡⲏ (λύπη) 'lupē/sorrow.' Possibly Lyc form related to ⲡⲕⲏ/ⲡⲱϣ-ⲛϩⲏⲧ 'distress, division of heart.'
Parsed as ⲛ̄-ⲥ-(ⲛⲁ)-ⲣ̄-ⲁⲡⲁⲛⲧⲏ 'and they shall encounter' — Greek ἀπαντάω 'meet, encounter' as Coptic verb with ⲣ̄- prefix. The lacuna at end likely contained the object encountered.
Translated 'or yet again is.' ⲏ = Greek 'or'; ⲁⲉ = Lyc ⲇⲉ 'and/again'; ⲟⲉ uncertain — possibly ⲟⲛ 'again' or qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱ 'be, exist.' The whole introduces the alternative locus of disturbance.
Translated 'mixture of bitterness.' ⲧⲱⲍ = Lyc ⲧⲱϩ 'mix, mingle' substantivized; the bitterness mingles with the body's faculties through the food. Cosmological-physiological mingling.

Translated 'a lowly counsel.' ⲥⲁⲭⲛⲉ = 'counsel' (fourth of the five faculties); ⲭⲁⲃⲁⲁⲧ qualitative — in glossary as 'latter/abandoned'; here in moral register modifying 'counsel' I render 'lowly/abased' since the counsel is what brings the bitter members in upon the body.
Translated 'passes over.' Standard ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ 'pass, transfer' (cf. accumulated ⲟⲩⲁⲧⲃⲉ 'be exalted'); here with directional ⲁ- 'to' = 'passes over to (becomes the cause of).'
Translated 'I have made known unto thee.' Per glossary entry ⲁⲧⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲉ 'make known/reveal'; standard apostolic teaching-formula.

Translated 'being established.' 3sg.f circumstantial of ⲥⲁⲧϩ̄ 'be set, established.' The food is 'established' in the body in the favorable case (when the powers above are still), in contrast to its disturbance in the bitter case.

Translated 'the air of above.' ⲁⲏⲣ = Greek ἀήρ; ⲡⲕⲉ- here is article with emphasis 'and the air also' or simply 'the air.' Cosmological register: the upper air being still allows the icon to be at rest.

Translated 'freshness' tentatively. The lexeme is unattested in our corpus; Crum offers ⲗⲁⲓⲃⲉⲥ 'shadow' but this does not fit the food/light-of-souls context. Best candidates: 'freshness/sap' (vegetative living-substance) or 'savor.' Confidence low.

Translated 'has soared (forth).' The construction parallels line 12-13 where the soul ⲁⲥⲓⲱⲟⲩ ⲁⲣⲁⲕ ⲉⲥⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲗⲉ ⲙ̄ⲡⲣⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲟⲩⲍⲁⲗⲏⲧ 'has soared unto thee, mounted in the manner of a bird,' establishing motion-upward semantics. Possible analysis: ⲁⲥ-ⲉⲓ-ⲱⲟⲩ '(she) has come (in) glory' or compound-stem 'soar/take flight.' 'Soared' preserves the bird-imagery.

Translated 'the slack thoughts.' ⲝⲁⲃⲁⲁⲧ qualitative on ϫⲱⲃ̄ 'be weak, slack' (Lyc ⲝ for ϫ). Context (paired with ⲉⲧϣⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'disturbed,' coming from evil counsels and deceitful teachings) supports a negative-deficient sense. Alternative 'defiled' from ϫⲱϩⲙ̄ less likely phonetically.
Translated 'deceitful teachings.' ⲍⲗⲃⲏⲧ likely from ϩⲱⲗⲃ̄/ϩⲁⲗⲃⲏⲧ family of 'deceit, falsehood' words. Distinguishes these counter-teachings from the true ⲛⲉⲕⲥⲃⲁⲩⲉ in line 11.

Both phrases translated 'these wells of those of the lower place.' Per glossary entry ⲁⲓⲍⲙⲉ 'well/spring' and ⲡⲥⲁⲙⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ 'lower side.' The variant ⲛⲁⲧⲓⲧⲉ in line 22 is a contracted/dialectal form of ⲛⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ.

Translated 'the bitter members.' ⲍⲁⲥⲉ likely Lyc variant of ϩⲁϫⲉ/ⲥⲁϣⲉ 'bitter' — pair-partner with ⲡⲙⲉⲗⲟⲥ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲓⲧ 'beautiful members' (line 1). Direct correspondence with the Manichaean food-typology of bitter (dark) vs. beautiful (light) members.
Translated 'bad-eating.' Compound: ⲃⲓⲛ ('bad, evil') + ⲟⲩⲱⲙ ('eat'). Names food unfit for the elect — the bitter-food register that brings disturbance through the lower wells.

Translated 'being firm, being select.' ⲧⲁⲕⲣⲉ qualitative likely from ⲧⲁⲕⲣⲟ/ⲧⲁϫⲣⲟ 'be firm, established.' ⲥⲁⲧϩ̄ tentatively from ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ qualitative ⲥⲟⲧⲡ̄ 'chosen, select' — describing the proper food which sustains rather than disturbs. Confidence moderate.

Translated 'gentleness' parallel to glossary ⲙⲛⲧⲍⲁⲗⲟⲏⲧ 'gentleness/mild-heartedness.' The disciple's response affirms that the apostle teaches them ⲍⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲁⲗⲃⲏⲧ 'in gentleness' — characteristic Manichaean pastoral virtue. Variant ⲍⲁⲗⲃⲏⲧ vs. ⲍⲁⲗⲟⲏⲧ may be dialectal.
